Subject: Pricing for private VPC + support tiers (Acme evaluation)

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for taking the call earlier. To recap, Acme is evaluating a private VPC deployment of Redwood for our customer-facing recommender (low latency, P95 < 200ms). Procurement asked me to get a clear breakdown on commercials before we proceed to legal. Key items we need:

- One-time platform/setup fee (what drives this vs a single SKU?)
- Recurring platform fee (monthly/annual) and whether that amortizes across committed capacity
- Support tiers (response times, number of incidents, on-call escalation) and cost deltas
- Migration assistance / runbooks and whether it's included or add-on
- Any volume discounts for a 2-year commit and how that affects the platform fee vs per-token/throughput pricing

If you can send a simple table or a short proposal that separates the "platform fee" from compute/usage SKUs, that would be ideal for our procurement team. Also, SOC2 evidence or an attestation would help speed the security review.

Best,
Jordan

Hi Jordan —

Thanks, and great to hear this is progressing. Attached is a short fee breakdown and an FAQ that should map to the procurement checklist you described. High level answers here:

- Platform/setup fee: one-time onboarding fee that covers VPC peering setup, private control-plane provisioning, initial performance tuning, and a migration planning block. Typical range is $50k–$120k depending on node count and data egress complexity; see attached pricing_sheet_v3.pdf for a sample mapping.
- Recurring platform fee: a fixed monthly fee that covers the control plane, telemetry retention (90 days by default), and platform features (console, rollouts, cost analytics). This is separate from Dedicated compute/throughput SKUs and is billable even when using Private.
- Support tiers: Standard (business hours, 24h SLAs on P1), Premium (24/7, 4h P1, 8x5 engineering access), and Enterprise (dedicated TAM, on-call rotation, quarterly on-site or virtual ops reviews). Pricing deltas are in the sheet.
- Migration assistance: we offer a 40-hour migration package included in onboarding for basic migrations; more complex lift-and-shift or on-prem air-gapped installs are scoped as billable add-ons.
- Discounts: we can do tiered discounts for 2-year committed spends — typically a discount applied against the platform fee and a separate committed usage rebate on compute.

Two quick clarifying questions for procurement:
1) Do you prefer the platform fee amortized monthly across the term (we can show both a one-time and amortized view)?
2) Are you planning an on-prem air-gapped installation or VPC with customer-managed NAT (that changes the migration scope)?

I pasted the core table below and attached the full sheet. If it helps I can pull Ben (who owns dedicated deals) into the thread for discounting options.

Attachments: pricing_sheet_v3.pdf

Thanks,

Jordan —

Looping in some commercial detail so procurement has something concrete to evaluate. We're open to structuring the commercial two ways:

Option A (Simpler):
- One-time onboarding: $75,000
- Platform fee: $6,500/month (baseline console, telemetry retention 90d)
- Support: Premium at +$15k/month (24/7 with 4h P1)
- Compute/throughput: quoted separately by expected peak RPS and model size
- 2-year commit: 12% discount on platform fee year 1, 15% year 2; 8% committed usage rebate on compute

Option B (More flexible):
- One-time onboarding: $95,000 with 6 months of platform fee waived (applies to larger node counts)
- Platform fee: $7,500/month after waiver
- Support: Enterprise add-on with TAM + on-call (custom pricing)
- 2-year commit: negotiable larger discounts in exchange for a higher minimum monthly committed usage

On compliance: we can provide a SOC2 summary and evidence package under an NDA; SOC2 report can be shared via our secure share.

If you can share an expected spend profile (monthly committed throughput and target SLOs) I can run the model and propose a recommended option. We're happy to move to a simple contract and SOW once procurement confirms the preferred commercial structure.

Best,
Ben Carter
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Pricing for private VPC + support tiers (Acme evaluation)

Kimberly / Ben —

Thanks for the options, that helps. Procurement shared a few constraints and asks before they can sign off:

1) Platform fee: they want the platform fee capped or partially waived for year 1 given we are committing to reserved throughput. Can Redwood do a cap of $60k for Y1 platform fees for a 2-year commitment?
2) Migration assistance: we need 80 hours of migration + runbook creation included for an air-gapped pilot. Will that be billable?
3) Support SLAs: Acme requires a guaranteed 99.9% platform availability SLA in the contract and a 10% credit per incident above SLA. Is that standard?
4) Compliance: procurement requires SOC2 Type II and an engineer contact for security callbacks during the audit review.

If you can send an updated term sheet that reflects a capped Y1 platform fee and the migration block, procurement can take to legal.

Jordan

Jordan —

Appreciate the clarity; we can meet most of these asks inline and I've attached an updated SOW and a priced term sheet for procurement. Summary of concessions and commitments below:

- Platform fee: capped at $60,000 for Year 1 for a signed 24-month commitment (we'll amortize the cap monthly on the invoice). Year 2 platform fee will be the agreed recurring rate less the contractual 12% committed discount.
- Migration assistance: include 80 hours of migration + runbook creation (SOW line item) at no additional charge for the pilot. Additional migration hours will be scoped as change orders.
- Support SLA: We will commit to a 99.9% platform availability SLA for the control plane; incident credits will follow our standard SLA schedule (10% credit for qualifying incidents above SLA) — legal can review the exact credit cap.
- Compliance: attached is the SOC2-evidence-summary.zip (redacted). We will provide a named security reviewer and coordinate an NDA for full report access.
- Discounting: final commercial model in the attached pricing sheet reflects the capped Y1 platform fee and a 10% average discount on compute for the 2-year commit.

Attachments: SOW-Acme-v1.docx; pricing_sheet_v3.pdf; SOC2-evidence-summary.zip
